newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight dips to 5.8/9 pct on fresh liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight dips to 5.8/9 pct on fresh liquidity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate dipped to 5.8/9 percent, the central bank's perceived floor level, as liquidity improved from 7.0/50 percent, dealers said on Tuesday.

They said the reason for the sharp dip in the overnight was not clear, it was possible that some institutions like finance companies and merchant banks, which are traditionally short, were well covered.
"I am not sure why the overnight fell so much. But, certainly there are some fresh funds in the market," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
Dealers said it was possible that Bank Negara injected funds into the banking system, but no confirmation was available. Bank Negara does not comment on its money market operations.
Earlier, most interbank rates remained steady, but under pressure to ease on expectations of a further improvement in liquidity, dealers said.

They said maturity of a 420 million long-term government bond on Wednesday and a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Friday would relieve some of the tightness the market has been experiencing over the last few weeks.
"Probably in anticipation of those maturities, people are holding back, waiting for rates to fall further," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue last Friday had triggered the easing process in the interbank market.
At the end of the morning session, one-week money was at 6.90/7.10 percent, two-week at 7.00/20 percent and three-week at 7.10/25 percent, all unchanged from Monday, when the rates fell sharply.
Other rates were also steady. One-month money ended at 7.20/25 percent, three-month at 7.25/30 percent and six-month at 7.30/35 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were higher across the board as investors continued to square up their positions, futures dealers said.
The benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up two points at 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
But, September was up two at 92.68, or 7.32 percent, and December up two at 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
